text: Ask "music or quiet?" Keep any music low, and if a song seems to be making things worse, change it. This is a bad time to defend the playlist. Talk slowly and say less, and please don't explain the universe at somebody who is already frightened by it. Have water there for them, and if they drink, get them to sip rather than chug, since a lot of water fast is dangerous on MDMA.
section: Psychological First Aid: The First Five Minutes
reader: someone looking after a person in a frightening psychedelic or MDMA state, in the first few minutes, once the immediate dangers (keys, stove, roads, more of the substance) are dealt with

sentences.s: Keep any music low, and if a song seems to be making things worse, change it.
sentences.payoff: the helper learns to keep any music low and to change a song that seems to be making it worse
sentences.follows: what to do with the music once they've answered

sentences.s: This is a bad time to defend the playlist.
Talk slowly and say less, and please don't explain the universe at somebody who is already frightened by it.
sentences.payoff: the helper learns how to talk: slowly, saying less, and no big explanations of the universe to someone it already frightens
sentences.follows: after the music, the helper's own voice, the other sound in the room

sentences.s: Have water there for them, and if they drink, get them to sip rather than chug, since a lot of water fast is dangerous on MDMA.
sentences.payoff: the helper learns to have water there without pressing it, and, if the person drinks, to get them to sip, because a lot of water fast is dangerous on MDMA
sentences.follows: the last thing the helper offers; the paragraph ends on why sipping matters

checked.point: a lot of water fast is dangerous on MDMA
checked.found: MDMA raises antidiuretic hormone while people drink heavily, which can drop blood sodium (hyponatremia), with seizures and brain swelling; the guide's MDMA section and its sodium warnings already rest on this
checked.still_needed: yes: it is why sipping matters, which a fresh reader asked

placement: after the room paragraph, in one paragraph: the music (his paragraph), then how to talk, then water (what was left of his fixes paragraph, in his words)

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first; a study after the question it answers)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine)
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
question_text.Q9: Is anything compressed? (one step a sentence, the small words that carry the relation, no space before mg)
